summary: Al From met with Governor Bill Clinton in Little Rock and charged him with transforming the Democratic Party's fortunes.
Bill Clinton secured Democratic support for a deficit-reduction budget combining immediate tax increases with phased spending cuts, with Al Gore casting the deciding vote.
Bill Clinton’s welfare law included time limits, setting a five-year limit on welfare benefits.

The House of Representatives was due to reconvene to complete its debate and vote on four impeachment charges against Bill Clinton, with the Republican majority expected to carry the day on each article.
Conservative Republican senators planned to launch an effort to derail a bipartisan deal that could end Bill Clinton's impeachment crisis.
The impeachment trial of President Bill Clinton opened in Washington.
Senators reached a bipartisan agreement to begin President Bill Clinton's impeachment trial next week while postponing the issue of whether to call witnesses.
The White House issued a formal rebuttal of the impeachment charges against Bill Clinton and abandoned the option to move for dismissal on constitutional grounds, resigned to a Senate trial.
The US Senate began the impeachment trial of President Bill Clinton on charges of perjury and obstruction of justice over his relationship with Monica Lewinsky.

President Bill Clinton delivered a televised State of the Union address to Congress, promoting his domestic agenda and announcing increased aid to Russia while his presidency continued amid the Senate impeachment trial.
White House lawyers told the Senate impeachment trial that President Bill Clinton was truthful in his federal grand jury testimony that forms the basis of the perjury charge against him.

President Bill Clinton proposed in his State of the Union speech a plan to devote $2,700 billion in projected budget surpluses over 15 years to Social Security, including allowing investment of a portion of the funds in the stock market.

Congressional Democrats renewed pressure for an early end to Bill Clinton's Senate impeachment trial, buoyed by the perceived success of the White House lawyers' defence case and the president's State of the Union speech.

Republican senators sought to bring the presidential impeachment trial of Bill Clinton to an early end, with a handful publicly expressing unease as acquittal on perjury and obstruction of justice charges was widely seen as inevitable.
Republican and Democratic leaders in the US Senate deadlocked over the future course of Bill Clinton's impeachment trial, diminishing hopes that the trial could end by mid-February.
President Bill Clinton indicated that the United States would seriously consider participating in a NATO ground force to implement a Kosovo settlement.
Republican prosecutors told the Senate in closing arguments of Bill Clinton's impeachment trial that he should be dismissed from office for perjury and obstruction of justice.

Tony Blair and Bertie Ahern planned to enlist Bill Clinton to help resolve the deadlock between Sinn Fein and the Ulster Unionists over paramilitary weapons decommissioning, with Clinton expected to make phone calls within weeks.
The US Senate began private final deliberations in President Bill Clinton's impeachment trial, with votes on the two articles of impeachment expected later that week.
The US Congress acquitted President Bill Clinton of the two impeachment charges against him.
Bill Clinton visited Hope, Arkansas, to dedicate his birthplace as a national historic site amid renewed unsubstantiated rumors about his marriage.
President Bill Clinton telephoned Slobodan Milosevic to urge him to accept the Kosovo peace deal after ethnic Albanian negotiators agreed to sign it.
President Bill Clinton met separately with Northern Ireland leaders David Trimble and Gerry Adams in Washington to urge further compromises on implementing the Good Friday peace agreement.

Ten senior political figures in Bill Clinton's home state of Arkansas, including leading members of his own Democratic party, were indicted on 133 charges of political corruption involving attempts to obtain illegally up to $5m of state funds.
Bill Clinton told ethnic Albanian refugees that Russia is nearing agreement with G-8 nations on a military force to protect them once fighting stops in Kosovo.

Bill Clinton returned home after a two-day trip to Germany, stating there is a real peace process under way but warning it has no chance of a satisfactory conclusion unless allied unity and firmness are maintained.
President Bill Clinton praised the deal between NATO and Russia on Kosovo peacekeeping arrangements at the G8 summit in Cologne.
President Bill Clinton announced a new federal prescription drug benefit worth up to $2,000 a year for 39 million elderly Americans, the first in a series of new spending programs.
Bill Clinton urged the parties in the Northern Ireland peace talks to reach a deal, speaking with Tony Blair, David Trimble, and Gerry Adams as negotiations continued without a breakthrough.
Bill Clinton concluded his poverty-focused tour in Watts, Los Angeles, after visiting poor areas including Appalachia, the Mississippi Delta, and an Indian reservation in South Dakota.
President Bill Clinton joined other NATO and EU leaders in Sarajevo for an international summit aimed at building stability, prosperity, and democracy in the Balkans after the Kosovo crisis.

At the Sarajevo summit, President Bill Clinton warned that Serbia will remain isolated until it removes Slobodan Milosevic and offered nearly $700 million in US aid for post-war reconstruction in south-eastern Europe.

Bill Clinton met with Israeli Prime Minister Ehud Barak and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat in Oslo at a memorial ceremony for Yitzhak Rabin, after which he said the peace process had been revitalized.

Bill Clinton signalled his willingness to accept a deal linking payment of nearly $1bn in unpaid US dues to the United Nations to restrictions on US aid for international family planning initiatives that support abortion.

President Bill Clinton cleared his diary to spend three days at the forthcoming World Trade Organization meeting in Seattle, prompting speculation he is prepared to push for a broader agenda than officially acknowledged.

President Bill Clinton and ministers from 135 countries made desperate efforts to save the global trade talks from collapse amid rioting in Seattle, with Clinton endorsing free trade while conceding negotiators had to listen to protesters' legitimate concerns.
Bill Clinton planned to use the final year of his presidency to promote "third way" politics and lay groundwork for promoting those ideas after leaving office.
Hillary Clinton vowed to spend the rest of her life with Bill Clinton, denying speculation that she would leave him after his presidency.
Bill Clinton delivered his eighth and final State of the Union address to a joint session of Congress, laying out numerous policy proposals.
Bill Clinton unveiled his Year 2001 budget proposals, projecting a debt-free US federal government by 2013.
A survey of 58 American historians ranked Bill Clinton 21st out of 41 U.S. presidents, placing him in the middle overall and last on moral authority.
President Bill Clinton told German chancellor Gerhard Schröder that the United States was prepared to support Horst Köhler as the new head of the IMF.
Bill Clinton met Hafez al-Assad in Geneva in a last-ditch effort to persuade him to restart peace talks with Israel, with no breakthrough announced.
Bill Clinton revealed plans to move in with his mother-in-law in Arkansas for a "couple of years" until the completion of his presidential library nearby.
At the Republican National Convention, Dick Cheney attacked Bill Clinton and Al Gore, saying it is time for them to go.

Bill Clinton was set to make his final convention speech at the Democratic National Convention in Los Angeles, defending his record and passing the torch to Al Gore.
Bill Clinton delivered a confident farewell speech at the Democratic National Convention and then flew to Michigan to pass the party standard to Al Gore.
A leak revealed that independent counsel Robert Ray had empanelled a grand jury in Washington to consider prosecuting Bill Clinton after he leaves office.
Bill Clinton continued a series of brief international visits, including stops in Egypt, Tanzania, Nigeria, and Colombia, in an effort to promote peace and bolster his foreign policy legacy.
President Bill Clinton opened the millennium summit with a call to better equip the UN to halt civil wars, eradicate poverty, and stop the spread of deadly diseases.
Al Gore is resisting pressure from strategists and candidates to deploy Bill Clinton on the campaign trail in the final stretch of the presidential race.

Bill Clinton arrived in Hanoi, becoming the first US president to visit Vietnam since the end of the Vietnam War.

Bill Clinton arrived in Ireland for his last foreign trip as US president.
Bill Clinton held talks in Belfast with Northern Ireland party leaders in a bid to push the peace process forward.
Bill Clinton's presidency ended as George W. Bush was inaugurated, with Bush having lost the popular vote and won Florida narrowly.
Bill Clinton left office as US president with a 65% approval rating, amid sharply divided assessments of his legacy.
The Bush administration placed a moratorium on implementing many of Bill Clinton's last executive orders.
The Clintons announced they were returning $28,000 worth of furnishings after donors discovered gifts intended for the White House had ended up in their Chappaqua home.
A senior US justice department official testified that none of the regular procedures were followed in Bill Clinton's presidential pardon of fugitive businessman Marc Rich.
Bill Clinton faced criticism over last-minute presidential pardons, including that of fugitive financier Marc Rich, amid questions about donations to his library fund and Democratic Party.

Bill Clinton's controversial pardons, including that of cocaine smuggler Carlos Vignali, became an issue in the Los Angeles mayoral election after it emerged that two leading candidates had lobbied the White House on Vignali's behalf.

Hillary Clinton became embroiled in the scandal over Bill Clinton's final day in office after it was revealed that her brother had received $400,000 for securing pardons for a convicted drug trafficker and a convicted swindler.
Bill Clinton arrived in Ireland for a four-day visit aimed at advancing the Northern Ireland peace process, with engagements in Belfast, Derry, Enniskillen, and Dublin.
Bill Clinton urged the people of Northern Ireland at a Derry rally to stick with the Good Friday agreement as the best chance for lasting peace.
Bill Clinton is to formally open the new Rothermere American Institute at Oxford University.
Bill Clinton was placed on standby to intervene in Northern Ireland emergency talks by phone if his involvement was felt to be helpful.
George Bush is poised to ask the US Congress to approve a White House budget request that would make Bill Clinton the first ex-American president to cost taxpayers more than $1m a year.
Bill Clinton opened his post-presidential headquarters in Harlem amid crowds of well-wishers and a small group of protesters.
Bill Clinton gave a lecture on globalisation at the London School of Economics and Political Science, focusing on the events of September 11.
Bill Clinton plans to build a full-scale replica of the Oval Office as the centerpiece of a permanent exhibition at the Clinton Presidential Center in Little Rock, Arkansas.
Bill Clinton warned Northern Ireland politicians to stand by the Good Friday agreement and "keep your eyes on the prize" and not turn back.
The University of Arkansas at Little Rock planned to offer a course on Bill Clinton's presidency beginning in January, described as the first of its kind.
Hillary Clinton revealed in her forthcoming memoir that Bill Clinton admitted his affair with Monica Lewinsky to her, describing her reaction and their subsequent marital difficulties.
Bill Clinton's 2000 visit to Ushafa, Nigeria, is cited as an example of unfulfilled US promises, as the computer centre, school, clean water and paved road he promised never materialized.
Bill Clinton announced that he had secured a deal with four generic drug companies to provide low-cost AIDS drugs in the developing world.
Bill Clinton brokered a deal with generic drug manufacturers to cut the price of HIV/AIDS drugs to 36 cents a day.
Random House announced it will publish Bill Clinton's memoir "My Life" at the end of June, though the text was not yet ready.
Bill Clinton's 957-page memoir My Life is set to go on sale in the US, drawing widespread reviews and media coverage.
Bill Clinton published his memoir "My Life."
Bill Clinton published his autobiography "My Life."
Bill Clinton is to appear on Channel 4's Richard and Judy to talk about his new autobiography.
John Kerry invited Hillary Clinton to give a primetime speech introducing her husband, Bill Clinton, on the opening night of the Democratic party convention.
Bill Clinton promoted his autobiography "My Life" in London with a book signing and a reception at the Guildhall.
Bill Clinton is scheduled to speak at the Democratic National Convention.
Bill Clinton joked at the Democratic National Convention about resenting talk of John Edwards's energy and intellect.
Bill Clinton delivered a speech at the Democratic National Convention that set the stage for John Kerry's acceptance speech.
Bill Clinton arrived in Belfast to meet Northern Ireland's political parties and encourage them to revive the suspended power-sharing assembly ahead of next month's negotiations.
Bill Clinton checked into a New York hospital for an emergency heart bypass operation after suffering chest pains.

Bill Clinton was recovering normally at a New York hospital after undergoing a quadruple bypass operation.
Bill Clinton was reported to be undergoing quadruple heart bypass surgery.
An audiobook review of Bill Clinton's autobiography "My Life" was published, criticizing the audio version as flat and less engaging than his in-person charisma.

Bill Clinton's presidential library was dedicated in Little Rock, Arkansas.
The Clinton Presidential Center, comprising a museum and library with the largest collection of presidential papers and artefacts in the US, was opening in Little Rock, Arkansas, to attract tourists.

Bill Clinton's office announced that he will undergo a medical procedure next week to remove scar tissue and fluid from around his heart.

Bill Clinton's Clinton Global Initiative began in Manhattan, convening about 800 people including roughly 50 world leaders to pledge money or action on poverty, religious strife, climate change, and governance.

Bill Clinton is praised by conservatives for signing the Welfare Reform Act into law 10 years ago, which ended welfare as Americans knew it.

Bill Clinton was nominated for the Grammy award for best spoken word album for his recording of Giving.

More than 70 Arkansas politicians and supporters who knew and worked with Bill and Hillary Clinton traveled to New Hampshire to campaign for Hillary Clinton.
Bill Clinton appeared alongside his daughter Chelsea at a campaign event in Iowa supporting Hillary Clinton after her third-place finish in the Iowa Democratic caucuses.
Bill Clinton campaigned across New Hampshire for his wife Hillary's presidential campaign, praising her as a practical problem-solver and "the best change maker" in American politics.

Barack Obama publicly confronted Bill Clinton over campaign attacks, accusing him of making troubling and factually inaccurate statements.
Bill Clinton criticized a reporter for raising the issue of race in the Democratic presidential contest while campaigning for his wife in South Carolina.

The Obama team threatened to retaliate in the Democratic presidential nomination race by exploring skeletons in the cupboard of former president Bill Clinton and his wife.

Bill Clinton defended Hillary Clinton's Bosnia anecdote at a campaign rally in Boonville, Indiana, saying critics overreacted and that she had been the first First Lady since Eleanor Roosevelt to go into a combat zone.

Bill Clinton over-reacted to a Vanity Fair article by calling its author "sleazy, slimy and dishonest," prompting Hillary Clinton's office to issue a statement that his language was inappropriate.
Bill Clinton’s reputation was damaged by his behavior during Hillary Clinton’s presidential campaign, and he reacted angrily to a Vanity Fair article about the Clinton post-presidency.
Gennifer Flowers and Paula Jones released a series of video clips titled "Two Chicks Chatting" in which they discussed the 1990s Clinton sex scandals.
Bill Clinton said through a spokesman that he is committed to helping Barack Obama become president.
Bill Clinton and Barack Obama spoke by phone and Clinton renewed his offer to campaign for Obama's presidential campaign.
Bill Clinton held his first extensive telephone conversation with Barack Obama since Hillary Clinton's defeat, a discussion seen as an important symbol of healing between the two camps.
Bill Clinton is slated to join pharmaceutical companies in New York to make a major announcement, likely related to his work on lowering the cost of life-saving drugs in the developing world.
Bill Clinton accepted an offer from the Obama campaign to speak at the Democratic National Convention on Wednesday, August 27, the night before the vice presidential nominee's speech.
Bill Clinton is expected to endorse Barack Obama at the Democratic convention despite a strained relationship and private reservations.
Bill Clinton is expected to endorse Barack Obama at the Democratic convention, though he reportedly feels little warmth toward Obama and relations with Obama's campaign team are brittle.
Bill Clinton publicly mused about a hypothetical "candidate X" who cannot deliver on Democratic issues, appearing reluctant to support Obama.
Bill Clinton delivered a speech at the Democratic National Convention endorsing Barack Obama for president and calling for party unity.
Bill Clinton endorsed Barack Obama for president in a speech at the Democratic National Convention.
Bill Clinton will skip Barack Obama's acceptance of the Democratic nomination.
Barack Obama met with Bill Clinton in New York for advice on how to fight back against a resurgent Republican presidential campaign.
Bill Clinton was set to hold his first rally for Barack Obama in Florida, marking his first general-election campaign appearance for Obama.

Democrats gained firm control of the White House, Senate, and House of Representatives for the first time since Bill Clinton headed the party's ticket in 1992.
Bill Clinton's global financial ties and foreign policy activities were discussed as potential conflicts if Hillary Clinton were selected as secretary of state.
Bill Clinton reportedly sent Barack Obama's transition team a list of more than 200,000 donors to his foundation to help clear the way for Hillary Clinton to become US secretary of state.

The William J Clinton Foundation released its donor list, disclosing nearly 200,000 contributors since its 1997 inception, after pressure from Barack Obama's transition team made Hillary Clinton's secretary of state nomination contingent on the disclosure.

During Hillary Clinton's Senate confirmation hearing for secretary of state, Republican senators raised concerns about a possible conflict of interest involving Bill Clinton's global fundraising, and Dick Lugar called on the former president to turn down all foreign donations to his foundation while his wife served as secretary of state.
Bill Clinton's 1993 inauguration was cited as having cost $33 million, far less than Barack Obama's 2009 inauguration.
The Senate was expected to acquit Bill Clinton on impeachment charges, as Republican support for conviction faltered.
Bill Clinton and UN secretary-general Ban Ki-moon arrived in Haiti for an overnight diplomatic visit including meetings with Haitian leaders and business figures.

Bill Clinton left North Korea with two freed US journalists after talks with Kim Jong-il, who pardoned the women.
The Clinton Tapes, Taylor Branch's book based on 79 secret recordings made with Bill Clinton during his presidency, was published.
Bill Clinton was rushed to a New York hospital and underwent a procedure to place two stents in one of his coronary arteries.
Bill Clinton left hospital after undergoing a successful procedure to open a blocked artery in his heart.

Bill Clinton returned to Little Rock, Arkansas for a two-day celebration marking the 20th anniversary of his 1991 presidential campaign announcement.

Barack Obama and Bill Clinton appeared together at three Manhattan fundraisers to raise money for Obama's re-election campaign.

Bill Clinton delivered a widely praised speech at the Democratic National Convention in Charlotte.
Bill Clinton declined to rule out a future Hillary Clinton presidential bid in 2016, saying he did not know what she would decide.
Bill Clinton said he had "no earthly idea" what Hillary Clinton might decide about a 2016 presidential run and praised her as a public servant.
Bill Clinton campaigned for Barack Obama at the University of Central Florida in Orlando, urging students to vote for Obama.

Bill Clinton headlined two fundraising events in Chicago for Hillary Clinton's presidential campaign, marking his first public appearance in support of her bid in this election cycle.

Bill Clinton returned to the campaign trail in Nashua, New Hampshire, making his first solo appearance of the 2016 election to endorse Hillary Clinton as the most qualified contender for the White House.
Bill Clinton defended his presidency to protesters who accused him and his wife of harming black communities with their crime and welfare policies.
